answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small, slashable deposit tied to one verified identity before trading, so spinning up thousands of fake agents becomes expensive instead of free. Reputation then accrues slowly over real completed work, like water carving a canyon: a newcomer starts at the horizon with no history, while a long-lived agent earns trust. A violet flag marks accounts whose behaviour suddenly diverges, letting peers pause dealings until the anomaly is explained.
